claim: In August 1969 the Railway Minister told Parliament that a Konkan line from Apta to Goa, costing about Rs 60 crore, could not be considered 'at present' because of the difficult ways-and-means (money) position and the need to save resources for priority projects.

evidence.locator: RS 11 Aug 1969, starred Q 464, answer (a) to (c)
evidence.quote: link may cost about Rs. 60 crores. Due to the
present difficult ways and means position and
priority projects, it is not possible to consider

notes: The earliest 'no' found on the record is about money, not about the line being impossible to build.

claim: Work on the first 62 km, Apta to Roha, had begun by June 1980, and that first stage opened in March 1986.

evidence.locator: RS 27 Jun 1980, unstarred Q 1171, answer (a) and (b)
evidence.quote: Konkan Railway by commencing the work on
the first 62 kmi. from Apta tQ Roha
Prof. Dandavate sanctioned the first stage from Apta to Roha, which was opened in March 1986

notes: 'kmi.' and 'tQ' are OCR errors in the scan. Month work began is not stated; say 'by 1980'.

claim: Konkan Railway Corporation Ltd was incorporated on 19 July 1990, and the foundation stone was laid at Roha on 15 September 1990.

evidence.quote: On July 19, 1990, Konkan railway Corporation Limited (KRCL) was incorporated
After the laying of the foundation stone at Roha by Mr.Sharad Pawar on September 15, 1990

notes: Sida says the project 'started in October 1990' (see conflicts.md); use the KRCL dates for the stone.

claim: The corporation was given four and a half years to build the line; both the builder and the Swedish evaluator later called that target unrealistic, Sida adding it was probably chosen partly for political reasons.

evidence.quote: Four and a half years were by no means realistic

evidence.locator: Sida Eval 97/25, ch. III Findings, 'output level' section
evidence.quote: the target date of 4 1/2 years was unrealistically optimistic, and probably chosen at least partly for political reasons

claim: The whole line, Roha to Thokur (near Mangaluru), opened for traffic on 26 January 1998, Republic Day: about 7 years 4 months after the foundation stone.

evidence.locator: KRCL Annual Report 2011-12, significant accounting policies, item iii
evidence.quote: The Broad Gauge line between Roha and Thokur was completed and opened for traffic on 26.1.1998.
the first train on the completed track was flagged off on January 26, 1998, Republic Day

notes: Duration computed in method/distance_and_arithmetic_output.txt: 15 Sep 1990 to 26 Jan 1998 = 2690 days = 7.36 years. Dedicated to the nation 1 May 1998 (coffee book) is a separate ceremony.

claim: As built, KRCL lists a route length of 738.941 km with 91 tunnels totalling 84.496 km (longest: Karbude, 6.5 km, near Ratnagiri) and 2,286 bridges, the longest 2,065.8 m across the Sharavati at Honnavar.

evidence.quote: Route Length 738.941km
Number of Tunnels 91 no. ( Total length 84.496 km)
Longest Tunnel 6.5km (Karbude Tunnel near Ratnagiri)
BRIDGES 2286
Longest Bridge (2065.8 m) Across Sharavati river in Honnavar

notes: Computed: tunnels are 11.4% of the route. Coffee book 2023 p.26 gives 2285 bridges; say 'over 2,000 bridges' or '2,286'.

claim: Sida's 1997 evaluation (Karlis Goppers) called it 'the biggest - and perhaps most difficult - railway undertaking during this century, at least in this part of the world'.

evidence.locator: Sida Eval 97/25, summary, 'The Konkan Railway construction project' para
evidence.quote: the project is the biggest - and perhaps most difficult - railway undertaking during this century, at least in this part of the world
the project is the biggest and perhaps most difficult railway undertaking during the century

notes: KRCL quotes Sida with small changes ('the century'). Quote Sida's own wording and attribute it.

claim: The hardest part was soft-soil tunnelling: nine soft-soil tunnels, mainly in Goa, caused the biggest cost increase and most of the delay; KRCL's chairman said tunnelling in such soil had not been done successfully anywhere in the world.

evidence.locator: Sida Eval 97/25, ch. III, cost escalation list
evidence.quote: the difficulties encountered in drilling through the nine soft soil tunnels
counted for the biggest cost increase, and the one which created most time delays
Tunneling in this kind of soil has not been done (successfully)

notes: The 'anywhere in the world' line is the chairman's (E. Sreedharan's) own claim as reported by Sida; attribute it to him. Sida adds that the record seems to back him. Sida also names the last two holdouts: Pernem and Old Goa tunnels.

claim: KRCL's own 2023 coffee-table book says E. Sreedharan took up the project at a time when 'all others' had called a railway in the region impractical; no person, report or date is named.

evidence.locator: KRCL Coffee Table Book 2023, p.224 'A Legacy' (flipbook OCR, columns merged)
evidence.quote: a time when all others had expressed
impracticality of constructing a railway

notes: This is the only source opened in which anyone says others thought it impractical; it is the builder's own anniversary book. Not a spine claim.

claim: The 'impossible' in the record is about money: Sida writes that it was felt impossible to raise Rs 10 billion for one project within the Indian Railways budget, which is why a separate corporation was set up.

evidence.locator: Sida Eval 97/25, ch. II, 'Independent Corporation' para
evidence.quote: would be impossible to raise 10 billion for just one project

notes: Can be added to the spine if the writer uses it; source and quote already verified.

claim: KRCL says the Konkan route cut Mangaluru-Mumbai rail distance from 2,041 km to 914 km (a saving of 1,127 km) and the journey from 41 to 15 hours.

evidence.locator: KRCL 'Salient Features', F. Savings in Distance
evidence.quote: Mangaluru - Mumbai 2041 914 1127

evidence.locator: same, G. Savings in Travel Time
evidence.quote: Mumbai -Mangalore 41 15 26

notes: KRCL's figures for the 1998 comparison; times are the builder's, not a current timetable.

evidence.quote: Where 100 km over easy territor y had taken 20 years
